Source: GIDEON Infectious Diseases of Rwanda 2015 Edition - Cholera in Rwanda
Description: GIDEON Informatics, 'Infectious Diseases of Rwanda', 2015 edition, pp.65-67, chapter 'Cholera in Rwanda'. A referenced compendium of Rwanda's cholera history compiled from WHO reporting and the published literature, with a per-year case and death graph and dated outbreak notes. Individual years: 1998 major activity in Cyangugu prefecture (Bushenge, Gihundwe, Kibogora and Mibirisi); 1999 major activity in Ruhengeri health region; 2007 '599 cases (13 fatal) were reported during January to February'. Notable outbreaks: 1987 Gisenyi Prefecture; 1994 an outbreak of 58,047 cases with at least 10,000 deaths 'in the wake of regional fighting'; 1996 Runda transit camp 106 cases 10 fatal; 1997 among Rwandan refugees in DRC; 2007 East Province and Western Province; 2009 'an outbreak (50 cases, 0 fatal) in the northwestern region'; 2013 'an outbreak (26 cases) at Nkombo Island'. CAUTION: the 1994 figure of 58,047 cases is the GOMA epidemic, which occurred in Zaire/DRC among Rwandan refugees and is counted against DRC in all standard sources - it is NOT Rwandan domestic incidence and must not be entered as such.
